title: Отменённый рейс и кофе у Шефа  (The Canceled Flight and Coffee at the Chef's)

segments.t: Out in the courtyard, Chef Barinov and Elena Pavlovna debate whose car to take until a sudden phone call informs Elena that her family's flight was canceled due to snow. With her apartment no longer free, she asks if they can have coffee at Barinov's place instead.
Мы на вашей машине поедем или на моей?
Может быть, к вам у вас есть кофе?
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
Мы на вашей машине поедем или на моей?
'Shall we take your car or mine?' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'we' and 'on' in a few short words.
'Does it not seem to you?' Notice the reflexive suffix on the verb meaning 'it seems', turning the action back on the subject. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Whatever you say.' In Russian, the idea of 'how' flows naturally into 'will you say' without extra filler words.
'Thank you, I can manage myself.' Notice how Russian expresses 'thank you' and 'himself' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'So whose car are we taking?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'like this' and finishing on 'whose'. Vika answers right away.
'Excuse me. Sorry.' In Russian, the idea of 'forgive' flows naturally into 'sorry' without extra filler words.
'My flights were canceled.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'by' and 'me' in a few short words.
'Because of snow or something.' The grammar packs 'then' and 'snow' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'So I am heading home.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'I' and finishing on 'home'.
'I understand.' Vika brings out the contrast between 'I' and 'understood' in a few short words.
'Coffee at my place is off.' Russian expresses 'having' with the preposition 'by' plus the genitive pronoun and 'is canceled'. Vika answers right away.
'Did something happen?' The grammar packs 'somehow' and 'to happen' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Может быть, к вам у вас есть кофе?
'Maybe we can go to your place, do you have coffee?' Notice how Russian expresses 'maybe' and 'coffee' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Let's hear the complete conversation once more.
Мы на вашей машине поедем или на моей?
Может быть, к вам у вас есть кофе?
